problem: The sentence after "The test is rank(Qo) = n" is broken: "If rank(Qo) o is square n×n and det(Qo) ≠ 0 proves observability." The condition for failure (rank < n means not observable) is lost and the p = 1 determinant shortcut is left grammatically attached to an orphan "o". A student cannot read what the failure condition is.
fix: "The test is rank(Q<sub>o</sub>) = n. If rank(Q<sub>o</sub>) < n, some state combination cannot be recovered from the output. For one output (p = 1), Q<sub>o</sub> is square n×n, so det(Q<sub>o</sub>) ≠ 0 proves observability."

where: Lead, Section 1, exam traps and quiz Q2
problem: "An−1B" and "CAn−1" are typed as plain text, so they read as A times n minus 1 times B rather than A to the power n−1 times B. The formula blocks use superscripts, so the notation is inconsistent inside the same chapter.
fix: Write A<sup>n−1</sup>B and CA<sup>n−1</sup> everywhere the block is spelled out in running text: Q<sub>c</sub> = [B  AB  A<sup>2</sup>B ... A<sup>n−1</sup>B] and Q<sub>o</sub> = [C; CA; ...; CA<sup>n−1</sup>].

problem: "One block proves nothing" is too strong. If B alone already has rank n (n independent inputs), the single block B does prove controllability.
fix: "Always form all n blocks before deciding; a single block can prove controllability only in the special case where B alone already has rank n, which is rare."

problem: It says "The figure after this section shows ...", but the figure is placed after Section 3, two sections later, so a reader looking just below Section 1 finds no figure.
fix: Say "The figure at the end of this chapter shows the two-state model used in the worked example ..." or move the figure directly after Section 1.
